1.summary: Paul thanks God for the Colossians' faith and love, prays they will be filled with knowledge of God's will, celebrates Christ as the image of the invisible God, creator and head of the church, who reconciled all things by his cross, and describes his own labor for the church.
1.lookfor: Notice the hymn about Christ in verses 15 to 20, and how many times "all" appears.

names.name: Colossae
names.gloss: A small town in the Lycus valley of Asia Minor, east of Ephesus.

names.name: Epaphras
names.gloss: A Colossian who brought the gospel to his own town.

insights.title: Faith, love, hope
insights.body: Paul thanks God for their faith in Christ and love for all the saints, because of the hope laid up in heaven (1:4-5). The same trio appears in 1 Corinthians 13.

insights.title: Epaphras
insights.body: The Colossians learned the gospel from Epaphras, a faithful servant (1:7). Paul likely sent co-workers from Ephesus to plant churches in Colossae, Laodicea and Hierapolis.

insights.title: The image of the invisible God
insights.body: Christ is the image, eikōn, of the invisible God (1:15). In him the unseen God becomes visible. Humans were made in God's image; Christ is that image perfectly.

insights.title: Firstborn
insights.body: Firstborn of all creation (1:15) doesn't mean first created; the next verse says all things were created through him. Firstborn meant rank and inheritance, as with Israel's king.

insights.title: Holding together
insights.body: All things were created through him and for him; he is before all things, and in him all things hold together (1:16-17). The one who made everything also sustains it.

insights.title: Peace by the cross
insights.body: Through him God reconciled all things to himself, making peace through the blood of his cross (1:20). The cross's reach is cosmic, as in Ephesians.

insights.title: Christ in you
insights.body: The mystery hidden for ages is now revealed: Christ in you, the hope of glory (1:27). The you is Gentile believers; Christ living among them is the proof of God's plan.

insights.title: Big enough
insights.body: Paul paints Christ as creator and sustainer of everything. Is the Jesus you trust as big as the one in this chapter?

2.summary: Paul warns against being taken captive by empty philosophy and human tradition, since all God's fullness dwells bodily in Christ; believers were circumcised in him, buried and raised with him, forgiven and freed, so they shouldn't submit to rules about food, festivals, visions or harsh treatment of the body.
2.lookfor: Notice the debt cancelled and nailed to the cross, and Paul's verdict on rules that look wise.

names.name: Laodicea
names.gloss: A wealthy city near Colossae, later addressed in Revelation.

insights.title: Rooted and built up
insights.body: As you received Christ Jesus the Lord, so walk in him, rooted, built up and established in the faith (2:6-7). The way you started is the way you continue.

insights.title: Elemental spirits
insights.body: Paul warns against philosophy according to the elements of the world (2:8), stoicheia, which could mean basic principles or spirits thought to rule the elements and stars.

insights.title: All the fullness
insights.body: In him all the fullness of the Godhead dwells bodily, and you are made full in him (2:9-10). Nothing needs to be added to Christ.

insights.title: The record of debt
insights.body: God cancelled the handwritten record of debt that stood against us, nailing it to the cross (2:14). The word cheirographon meant a signed IOU. Crucifixion notices were nailed above victims; here it's our debt that's nailed up.

insights.title: A public triumph
insights.body: Having stripped the rulers and authorities, he made a public spectacle of them, triumphing over them in the cross (2:15). The image is a Roman victory parade, the cross its chariot.

insights.title: Shadows and substance
insights.body: Food, drink, festivals, new moons and Sabbaths are a shadow of things to come; the body belongs to Christ (2:16-17). Why hold the shadow when you have the reality?

insights.title: Rules that don't work
insights.body: Don't handle, don't taste, don't touch (2:21). Such rules look wise and devout but have no value against indulging the flesh (2:23). Self-made religion can't change the heart.

insights.title: Adding rules
insights.body: The Colossians were tempted to add spiritual extras to Christ. What do you feel you need besides Christ to be right with God?

3.summary: Since believers have been raised with Christ, they are to set their minds on things above, put to death earthly vices and put on compassion, forgiveness and love, let Christ's word dwell in them richly, and live out their faith in households of wives and husbands, children and fathers, slaves and masters.
3.lookfor: Notice the lists of what to put off and put on, and the phrase "as to the Lord" in the household instructions.

names.name: Scythian
names.gloss: A people north of the Black Sea, regarded by Greeks as the most uncivilized.

insights.title: Hidden with Christ
insights.body: You died, and your life is hidden with Christ in God; when Christ appears, you will appear with him in glory (3:3-4). Identity is secure even when unseen.

insights.title: Put to death
insights.body: Put to death what is earthly: immorality, impurity, passion, evil desire, and covetousness, which is idolatry (3:5). Greed is named as idol worship, wanting things more than God.

insights.title: Barbarian, Scythian
insights.body: In the new humanity there is no Greek or Jew, circumcised or uncircumcised, barbarian, Scythian, slave or free (3:11). Barbarians were non-Greek speakers; Scythians were the stereotype of savages.

insights.title: Bond of perfectness
insights.body: Above all, put on love, which is the bond of perfection (3:14). Love is like a belt that holds all the other virtues together.

insights.title: Psalms, hymns and spiritual songs
insights.body: Let the word of Christ dwell in you richly, teaching and admonishing one another with psalms, hymns and spiritual songs (3:16). Singing is a way of teaching.

insights.title: As to the Lord
insights.body: Whatever you do, work heartily, as for the Lord and not for people (3:23). Paul addresses slaves directly as moral persons, and reminds masters they too have a Master (4:1).

insights.title: Put on
insights.body: Paul lists what to put on: compassion, kindness, humility, gentleness, patience (3:12). Which of these do you most need to put on today?

4.summary: Paul asks prayer for open doors and clarity, urges wise and gracious speech toward outsiders, and sends greetings from co-workers including Tychicus, Onesimus, Aristarchus, Mark, Epaphras, Luke and Demas, closing in his own hand: remember my chains.
4.lookfor: Notice the list of names, which shows the network around Paul, and the instruction to share letters between churches.

names.name: Tychicus
names.gloss: The co-worker who carried this letter.

names.name: Onesimus
names.gloss: A runaway slave from Colossae, now a faithful brother.

names.name: Mark
names.gloss: Barnabas's cousin, once a cause of division, now commended.

names.name: Luke
names.gloss: The beloved physician, author of Luke and Acts.

names.name: Demas
names.gloss: A co-worker who later deserted Paul.

names.name: Archippus
names.gloss: A believer urged to fulfill his ministry, probably of Philemon's household.

insights.title: An open door
insights.body: Paul, in chains, asks prayer not for release but that God would open a door for the word (4:3).

insights.title: Seasoned with salt
insights.body: Let your speech always be with grace, seasoned with salt (4:6). Salt preserved and gave flavor; Greek writers used salty for witty, engaging speech.

insights.title: Onesimus
insights.body: Onesimus, the faithful and beloved brother, who is one of you (4:9). He is the runaway slave of the letter to Philemon, returning home with Tychicus.

insights.title: Mark restored
insights.body: Paul sends greetings from Mark, Barnabas's cousin, and tells them to welcome him (4:10). Years earlier Paul had refused to take Mark; now he is a co-worker.

insights.title: Luke the physician
insights.body: Luke, the beloved physician, greets you (4:14). This is the only place Luke's profession is named; it's listed among co-workers not of the circumcision, so Luke was likely a Gentile.

insights.title: Swap letters
insights.body: When this letter has been read among you, have it read in the church of the Laodiceans, and read the letter from Laodicea (4:16). Letters circulated from the start; the letter from Laodicea is lost, or may be Ephesians.

insights.title: Remember my chains
insights.body: Paul signs with his own hand: remember my chains (4:18). The great vision of Christ's supremacy came from a prisoner.

insights.title: Second chances
insights.body: Mark failed once and was trusted again. Who might you need to give a second chance?

intro.who: Paul and Timothy (1:1), to a church Paul had never visited, founded by his co-worker Epaphras (1:7). Some scholars question Paul's authorship; many accept it.
intro.when: About AD 60–62, from prison, sent with Tychicus and Onesimus together with Philemon (4:7-9).
intro.why: A teaching was unsettling the church that mixed special knowledge, visions, angel worship, food rules and festivals. Paul answers that Christ is supreme over all creation and powers, and that in him believers already have fullness; nothing needs to be added.

outline.title: Fullness in Christ, not in rules
